newsitem.title: USA: ITT Corp. reports flat quarterly profits.
newsitem.headline: ITT Corp. reports flat quarterly profits.

text.p: ITT Corp. reported flat third-quarter profits of $67 million Friday, saying its hotel, entertainment and information businesses grew but its gambling earnings fell.
The New York-based company said its net income was equivalent to 57 cents per share, and compared with earnings of $67 million, or 56 cents per share, a year ago.
Revenues rose to $1.67 billion from $1.62 billion.
"The outlook for all of our businesses remains favourable," company Chairman Rand Araskog said in a statement.

"Our hotel, information services and entertainment businesses are exhibiting strong growth relative to 1995 and are well positioned in their markets. As previously announced, our gaming results came under pressure during the quarter," he said.
The stock of ITT, formed last December in the breakup of the former multinational company of the same name, rose 62.5 cents to $42.75 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
In hotels, ITT Sheraton generated earnings before interest, taxes and other items of $125 million, a 44 percent increase over 1995's $87 million.

In its information services division, operating earnings were $72 million vs. $65 million a year ago, which the company said reflected improved performance at its directories and educational services businesses.

But gambling operating earnings dropped to $76 million from $106 million a year ago as revenues from its Las Vegas properties dropped substantially, ITT said. In addition, construction at the Desert Inn in Las Vegas and increased competition among casinos in Tunica, Miss., also hurt results.

"As we execute our major gaming expansion and renovation programme in Las Vegas and Atlantic City, the 1997 gaming results could continue to be affected by construction disruption," Araskog said. "We expect these programmes to generate significant growth in the gaming segment."
